question: Financing of UNRWA by the European Union and allegations of involvement of UNRWA employees in Hamas’ attack on Israel of 7 October 2023

Several staff members of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) are alleged to have been involved in Hamas’ attack on Israel of 7 October 2023, which left more than 1 200 Israelis dead and provoked a war in Gaza.

In response, seven EU Member States have announced they will halt payments to UNRWA pending investigations, as have the US, the UK, Switzerland and Canada. The EU, the largest donor of humanitarian and development assistance to Gaza, has quadrupled its payments of humanitarian aid since the war between Israel and Hamas broke out in October 2023.
Following the allegations, the Commission announced that it would ‘review’ its support to UNRWA and stop planned additional funding until the end of February 2024. 1.
In the light of the above allegations, does the Commission believe that UNRWA is able to fulfil the tasks arising from its mandate?

Taking into account the above, as well as previous irregularities in the operation of UNRWA, what specific measures does the Commission intend to take to prevent the misuse of EU money by this organisation and, in particular, to prevent its staff’s involvement in terrorist activities?
answer: The EU has expressed grave concern with regards to the very serious allegations made on 24 January 2024 against 12 United Nations Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA) staff members. The Commission has welcomed the United Nations’ (UN) Office for Internal Oversight Services investigation to shed light into the serious allegations against UNRWA staff.

Furthermore, it has commended the UN for creating an independent Review Group led by former French Minister Catherine Colonna to assess whether the Agency is doing everything within its power to ensure neutrality and respond to allegations of serious breaches. The Commission is also in contact with the authorities of Israel on the matter.

The Commission has engaged with UNRWA’s Commissioner General Lazzarini and welcomed his commitment to tackle the serious issues at stake. Letters outlining the way forward with all the measures and procedures for the Commission’s conditional funding for UNRWA were exchanged on 1 and 6 March 2024.

The conditions for the disbursement of the first tranche were the following: agreement by UNRWA on the three workstreams (the screening of UNRWA staff; system audit; reinforcement of the Department of Internal Investigations and Ethics office) and the signature of the EU-UNRWA contribution agreement; declaration in writing by UNRWA that up-to-date, necessary and proportionate information on staff has been shared and will be done on a quarterly basis; and the adoption by UNRWA of a concept note detailing how to strengthen the Department of Internal Oversight Services, including the establishment of a new neutrality investigation unit, and Ethics office.

Following UNRWA’s fulfilment of these conditions, the Commission paid a first tranche of EUR 50 million out of the EUR 82 million foreseen for UNRWA for 2024. The second and third tranches of EUR 16 million are subject to the implementation of the agreement with UNRWA and the Agency’s compliance with the agreed conditions and milestones.

In line with sound financial management principles, the agreement with UNRWA foresees the possibility for the Commission to suspend or recover payments should credible information indicating significant deficiencies in the functioning of the internal control system come to light.
